- One-line purpose: vision_system's frame store in DDR (USE_DDR_FB), an AXI4 master of the shared DDR controller (ip/memory/ddr_ctrl).
- Version: 1.0.0

Reject illegal values at elaboration with `$error` inside a generate block.

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

- **m_axi_*** - AXI4 (full) master, address [AXI_ADDR_W-1:0], data [DATA_W-1:0]: discrete ports (bursts and IDs; the library has no full-AXI4 interface).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Widths are module parameters (Icarus has no $bits of an interface member); connect `.p(inst)`, not `.p(inst.mp)`. Yosys reads a top with interface ports through its discrete wrapper (`ip/scripts/syn_wrap.py`, sv2v); cocotb tests drive such a wrapper's plain ports.

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
vision_system's frame store in DDR (USE_DDR_FB), an AXI4
master of the shared DDR controller (ip/memory/ddr_ctrl). Version 2.0.0.
Golden model: model/ddr_frame_store_model.py (clock exact; tb/python,
with ddr_ctrl and ddr_mem).
- Two frame buffers in DDR at byte addresses BASE0 / BASE1 (wr_buf /
  rd_buf choose one per access); pixel a of buffer b is the 32-bit slot
  at BASE<b> + 4 a, the pixel in its low PIX_W bits (the rest 0). Every
  slot must lie in the memory behind the controller: BRESP / RRESP are
  not checked, read data is used as returned.
- Writes (wr_en with wr_ready): a combiner gathers the pixels of one
  DATA_W word (PPB = DATA_W / 32 slots, byte strobes per slot). A write
  to another word pushes the gathered word into the write queue
  (fallthrough_fifo, WQ_DEPTH words) and starts the next; a word with
  every slot written is pushed at once; a partial word is pushed after
  FLUSH_IDLE clocks without a write (with room in the queue). wr_ready =
  the queue is not full. Each queued word is one single-beat AXI write
  (AWLEN 0, full size, INCR, AWID WR_ID, WLAST 1): AW and W presented
  together, each dropped at its handshake; the next word is loaded once
  both have gone, while fewer than OUT_MAX writes wait for B (BREADY 1).
  wr_idle = nothing gathered, queued, presented or waiting for B.
- Reads (rd_en with rd_ready): a direct-mapped cache of CACHE_LINES lines
  of LINE_PIX pixels (line = slot index >> log2(LINE_PIX), set = line mod
  CACHE_LINES, tag = line / CACHE_LINES), its RAM in four copies (one
  synchronous read port per address, every copy written by a fill). The
  request in lookup looks its four addresses up every clock: each that
  hits and is not yet read is read from its copy (the word the next
  clock, the pixel captured then); a miss loads the line of the first
  address neither read nor hitting, with one AXI read burst of LINE_PIX /
  PPB beats (ARID RD_ID, full size, INCR; RREADY 1 while loading), each
  beat written as it arrives, valid after the last; the lookups go on
  (addresses already read are kept: two addresses whose lines share a set
  never evict each other forever). The request completes in the clock its
  last addresses are read; the clock after, rd_valid pulses with
  rd_data0..3 (registers). rd_ready = no request in lookup, or the one in
  lookup completing this clock: one request per clock while the lines are
  cached, 3 clocks from a request to its rd_valid, requests answered in
  order (vision_system's output at a pixel per clock, as its on-chip
  store).
- rd_flush (taken with rd_ready, before a request in the same clock):
  every line becomes invalid. The cache does not see writes: pulse
  rd_flush after a rewritten buffer is complete (wr_idle), before
  reading it.
- clear (the user's soft reset, e.g. vision_system's CTRL[0]): the read
  request in lookup is dropped without rd_valid, at once, or after the
  last beat of its line fill (an AXI burst is always completed), and so
  is the rd_valid of a request completed the clock before; rd_en is
  ignored in that clock. Writes and the cache lines
  are not affected.
Every output is a register or a function of registers.
Parameters: PIX_W (<= 32), ADDR_W (pixel address bits), DATA_W (AXI data,
power of two >= 64), AXI_ADDR_W, ID_W, BASE0 / BASE1, LINE_PIX /
CACHE_LINES / WQ_DEPTH (powers of two >= 2; LINE_PIX 2 .. 256 beats of
PPB pixels and at most 1024 pixels: a line fill never crosses 4 KB),
FLUSH_IDLE / OUT_MAX (1 .. 255), WR_ID / RD_ID.
Clock - clk (the controller's). Reset - synchronous active low rst_n,
the controller's reset (asserted with it, so that no AXI transaction is
abandoned; the cache RAM keeps its contents). Clock-domain crossings -
none.
Resources - the cache RAM 4 x CACHE_LINES x LINE_PIX x PIX_W bits, the
queue WQ_DEPTH x (AXI_ADDR_W + 9 DATA_W / 8) bits. Errors - none
reported.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - ddr_frame_store (2026-10-26, version 2.0.0)
// Sources:
//   [1] Arm, "AMBA AXI and ACE Protocol Specification" (IHI 0022, issue H), https://developer.arm.com/documentation/ihi0022
//   - A3.3.1 handshakes (a master must not wait for READY before VALID; AW and W may be presented
//   together), A3.4 INCR bursts, sizes, the 4 KB boundary rule, write strobes (A3.4.3)
//   [2] AMD/Xilinx, "AXI Video Direct Memory Access (VDMA)" PG020 - frame buffers in external memory,
//   multiple buffers (park / circular), the writer and reader on separate buffers (no tearing)
//   [3] J. L. Hennessy, D. A. Patterson, "Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach", 6th ed.,
//   appendix B - direct-mapped caches (index / tag / valid, line fills on a miss)
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   Double-buffered frame store: the writer fills one buffer while the reader reads the other, the
//   buffers swap at frame boundaries once the written frame is complete [2]; a read path with random
//   access uses a cache of lines (index = line mod sets, tag = line / sets) loaded by burst reads [3];
//   AXI writes as full-width words with byte strobes for the bytes written [1].
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: two buffers chosen per access (the sequencer swaps them, as VDMA's circular mode with two
//   frames), writes gathered into full-width words with per-slot strobes, single-beat INCR writes,
//   line fills as one INCR burst of LINE_PIX / PPB beats aligned to the line, so a fill never
//   crosses 4 KB (LINE_PIX <= 1024, 4 KB of 32-bit slots, checked at elaboration),
//   AW and W presented together (legal [1]); direct-mapped cache with tags over the whole slot
//   address (both buffers share it without aliasing); the four taps of a request read in one clock
//   from four copies of the cache RAM (a multi-ported cache by replication [3]), so the reader keeps
//   up with a pixel per clock while its lines are cached.
//   Simplifications (deliberate): one outstanding read burst (the lookups wait for its line); the cache
//   does not snoop writes (the sequencer flushes it at a frame swap, documented); responses not
//   checked (the buffers are configured inside the memory); 32-bit pixel slots (no 24-bit packing:
//   simpler addressing at 33 % more memory, which the architecture study does not constrain).
// Result: in line with the reference; no TODO.
```


## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: report the Yosys utilisation; keep it in line with similar library blocks.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking directed testbench of ddr_frame_store on a
one-port ddr_ctrl with ddr_mem (256-bit words, 20 x 12 frames, 8-line
cache of 32 pixels, T_REFI 300). Checks, independently of the Python
model (a pixel scoreboard per buffer): a frame written in raster order
with gaps reads back in bilinear and bicubic neighbourhoods; writes to
one buffer while the other is read (double buffering) leave the read
frame intact; a rewritten buffer reads back its new frame after wr_idle
and rd_flush, and its old frame without the flush (the cache does not
see writes, as specified); scattered single-pixel writes (partial words)
land; wr_idle falls with a write and rises once it is in memory; a
clear during a line fill drops the request (no rd_valid; the store
ready again once the burst is complete, the next read correct); and
ddr_mem reports no timing violation. +define+MUTATE corrupts one
expected pixel: the testbench must then fail (mutation check). Test
tasks in tests/ddr_frame_store_tests.sv. Prints TEST PASSED and
>>> PASS <<< on success.
```

There is also a Python (cocotb) test in `tb/python/`; provide an equivalent.

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `the simulation script --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `tb_ddr_frame_store` | `test_write_read` | A frame into buffer 0, read back in bilinear and bicubic neighbourhoods |
| `tb_ddr_frame_store` | `test_double_buffer` | Buffer 1 written while buffer 0 is read: the read frame stays intact |
| `tb_ddr_frame_store` | `test_rewrite_flush` | A rewritten buffer reads its old (cached) pixel without rd_flush, the new one with it |
| `tb_ddr_frame_store` | `test_scattered_writes` | Single pixels at scattered addresses (partial words) read back after wr_idle and rd_flush |
| `tb_ddr_frame_store` | `test_wr_idle` | wr_idle falls with a write, rises once it is in memory |
| `tb_ddr_frame_store` | `test_clear` | clear during a line fill drops the request; the next request is answered |
| `tb_ddr_frame_store` | `test_timing_kept` | ddr_mem reported no timing violation |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: the block's `scripts/run.sh` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, synthesis passes.
